decisions.summary: Three-bead decomposition: (1) patrol-scope filter in reconcileFalseMerged, (2) one-shot 401 retry in githubApi, (3) module-level circuit breaker with 5-min TTL and single actionable log.

The patrol-scope filter uses the same cached `gh issue view --json state,labels` pattern as `getAutoCloseOutCanonicalState` in deacon.ts:3766. Skip issues whose canonical state is `done` or `canceled`. Reuse the existing `autoCloseOutCache` (10-min TTL) rather than introducing a parallel cache.

The 401 retry is scoped to the private `githubApi<T>` helper in src/lib/github-app.ts only (3 in-file callers). Direct-fetch sites `mergePullRequestWithAppPromise` and `reportCommitStatus` are NOT modified — they are out of the reported symptom path (patrol false-merged check) and not part of the 60s patrol cadence that causes log spam.

Circuit breaker is module-level state in github-app.ts (`appDegradedUntil: number`, `appDegradedLogged: boolean`). 5-minute TTL = 5 patrol cycles. Self-clearing — no admin command required to reset for transient failures.

Diagnostic recovery command in the breaker's error message is `node scripts/create-github-app.mjs` (with the `PANOPTICON_DEV_WEBHOOKS=1` env gate the script enforces). The issue text suggests `pan admin github-app refresh` but no such CLI verb currently exists; pointing at the truthful, existing path is preferable to inventing a command.

Only HTTP 401 triggers the retry — 403/404/5xx preserve the existing single-shot error path. Rationale: 401 specifically indicates token rejection; 403 means token is accepted but lacks permission (retry won't help); 404 means resource is gone (retry won't help); 5xx is a server issue (different retry policy, out of scope).

Implementation and unit tests are bundled per bead (3 beads instead of 6). Splitting impl from tests would create un-shippable beads (impl with no coverage in main briefly). Each bead is independently mergeable as a complete impl+test unit.

hazards.summary: `githubApi` is module-private with only 3 in-file callers — but tests must not accidentally exercise the network. Tests must mock the global `fetch` via `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...)` or similar, not hit api.github.com.
hazards.mitigation: Vitest pattern: `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn())` in beforeEach with returnValueOnce sequences for the 401 → retry → 200/401 paths. Also stub `loadGitHubAppConfig` to return a synthetic config so the JWT-signing path doesn't try to read ~/.panopticon/github-app/private-key.pem.

hazards.summary: The breaker's 5-min TTL and the log-once semantic interact with test isolation. If two tests in the same file open the breaker, the second test's 'first log' check will fail because module state persists across tests.
hazards.mitigation: Add an internal `__resetGitHubAppBreakerForTests()` export (or a test-only hook), and call it in `beforeEach`. Project rule (CLAUDE.md): use `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync()` for the TTL-expiry test — NOT real setTimeout.

hazards.summary: `reconcileFalseMerged` runs every 60s. Adding a `gh issue view` shell-out per non-cached issue could be slow on first patrol after a server restart (the autoCloseOutCache is in-memory and cleared on restart). For a typical deployment with <100 merged-status issues, the worst case is ~100 sequential `gh issue view` calls — bounded but not free.
hazards.mitigation: Reuse the existing `withConcurrencyLimit` pattern from `autoCloseOut` (deacon.ts:3839) if the per-patrol cost becomes noticeable. For the initial implementation, sequential is fine (matches `getAutoCloseOutCanonicalState`'s current call pattern). If the cache key matches `autoCloseOutCache`, both reconcilers share the cost on first miss.

hazards.summary: Modifying `githubApi` to retry on 401 could mask configuration bugs in development. If an operator's installation-id is wrong, the retry won't fix it — they need the breaker to surface the diagnostic.
hazards.mitigation: The breaker's actionable log explicitly tells the operator how to recover. The retry only buys one transient-race recovery attempt; persistent 401s flow into the breaker exactly as intended.

hazards.summary: If `generateInstallationToken` itself throws (e.g. private-key.pem unreadable, App-id wrong), the 401-retry path never runs — the existing single-shot error path runs instead. That's fine for retry correctness, but means the breaker NEVER engages for that failure mode. The operator still sees errors but they look different (token-generation errors, not 401s).
hazards.mitigation: Out of scope for this issue — the reported symptom is 401-after-token-issued. Token-generation errors would be a separate bug (different error message, different recovery path). If the team wants the breaker to also trip on token-generation failures, that's a follow-up. Note in the implementation that this is intentional.

hazards.summary: The circuit breaker is process-local. A multi-process setup (Cloister + auxiliary workers) would each have their own breaker — operator sees the diagnostic log multiple times.
hazards.mitigation: Panopticon's deacon runs in a single dashboard server process. The 'Single Deacon Invariant' rule in CLAUDE.md confirms only one deacon exists per `~/.panopticon` state dir. So per-process is sufficient for the reported topology.
